318.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 318.

scenes.say: Bitcoin has moved in cycles of roughly four years. Here's why people watch them.
scenes.p: A giant golden clock with four seasons painted on its face and a Bitcoin coin as the hour hand, the wolf winding it.

scenes.say: So far, the pattern has been: a halving, a big bull run, a peak, then a deep bear market.
Each cycle lasted about four years, in line with the halving schedule.
But as big investors and ETFs arrive, the pattern may change, or fade.
Use cycles as context, not as a calendar to bet on.
Follow for part 319: robo-advisors. Not financial advice.
What if a robot managed your investments for a small fee?
scenes.p: A friendly robot in a suit sits across a desk from the wolf, presenting a neat portfolio pie chart on a tablet.

scenes.say: A robo-advisor is an app that builds and manages a diversified portfolio for you.
You answer questions about your goals and risk, and it picks a mix of low-cost funds.
It rebalances automatically, usually for lower fees than a human advisor.
Simple and cheap, but it can't understand your whole life. Check the fees and what's inside.
Follow for part 320: the biggest crypto crashes in history. Not financial advice.

320.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 320.

scenes.say: The biggest crypto crashes in history, in one minute.
scenes.p: A dramatic museum hall displaying giant red falling arrows like monuments, the wolf walking through as a tour guide.

scenes.say: In 2011, Bitcoin fell more than ninety percent in a few months.
After 2013 and the Mt. Gox collapse, it lost about eighty-five percent.
From the 2017 peak, it dropped over eighty percent. In 2022, more than seventy-five percent.
Every crash felt like the end. Survivors avoided leverage and never risked more than they could lose.
Follow for part 321: why Bitcoin dominance moves. Not financial advice.

321.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 321.

scenes.say: Why does Bitcoin's share of the crypto market keep changing?
scenes.p: A tug of war between a giant golden Bitcoin team and a colorful team of altcoins, the wolf as the referee.

scenes.say: When fear rises, money often flows back to Bitcoin, the most established coin.
When confidence is high, traders hunt for faster gains in altcoins.
Stablecoins and new coins also change the total market, which affects dominance.
It's a mood gauge for the whole market. Watch it, don't worship it.
Follow for part 322: financial independence and FIRE. Not financial advice.
Some people retire in their forties. They follow a movement called FIRE.
scenes.p: The wolf relaxes in a hammock on the porch of a peaceful mountain cabin while a small money tree grows next to him.

scenes.say: FIRE stands for financial independence, retire early.
The idea: save a big part of your income, invest it, and eventually live off the returns.
A common rule of thumb is reaching about twenty-five times your yearly expenses.
It takes years of discipline. Even if you never retire early, the habits make you freer.
Follow for part 323: the altcoin risk ladder. Not financial advice.

323.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 323.

scenes.say: Not all crypto carries the same risk. Picture a ladder.
scenes.p: A tall ladder against a wall: the bottom rungs are solid gold, the top rungs thin and cracked, the wolf climbing carefully.

scenes.say: At the bottom: Bitcoin and Ethereum, the most established.
Higher up: large altcoins, then mid caps, then small caps.
At the top: brand new tokens and meme coins. The higher you climb, the harder you can fall.
Keep most of your money near the bottom, and only a little near the top.
Follow for part 324: how new coins get listed. Not financial advice.

324.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 324.

scenes.say: How does a new coin end up on a big exchange?
scenes.p: A coin character waits in a long line in front of a grand exchange building with a velvet rope and a doorman.

scenes.say: Most new tokens first appear on decentralized exchanges, where anyone can list.
Big centralized exchanges are selective. They review the project, the team, and the risks.
Some projects pay listing fees or make deals, which aren't always public.
A listing isn't an approval. Do your own research either way.
Follow for part 325: passive income myths. Not financial advice.
Make money while you sleep. The internet loves that promise.
scenes.p: The wolf lies on a beach chair next to a laptop showing a money rain, while the desert behind him is clearly a cracking mirage.

scenes.say: Social media is full of passive income dreams: courses, dropshipping, crypto yields.
Most so-called passive income takes a lot of work at the start, or a lot of money.
Truly passive income usually comes from invested capital: dividends, interest, rent.
If someone sells you an easy passive income system, they're the one earning it.
Follow for part 326: do crypto protocols make money. Not financial advice.

326.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 326.

scenes.say: Do crypto protocols actually make money? Some do. Many don't.
scenes.p: The wolf examines a busy futuristic toll bridge where small coins drop into a glowing treasury chest.

scenes.say: Some earn real fees: exchanges, lending apps, and blockchains themselves.
That revenue can go to a treasury, to token holders, or to token burns.
Many other tokens have no revenue at all. Their price depends only on demand.
Ask two questions: does it make money, and does the token benefit from it?
Follow for part 327: token burns. Not financial advice.

327.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 327.

scenes.say: Some projects destroy their own coins on purpose. It's called a token burn.
scenes.p: The wolf throws a pile of glowing coins into a big fire pit, the flames turning golden.

scenes.say: A burn removes coins from circulation forever, by sending them to an address nobody can use.
Ethereum burns part of every transaction fee. Some exchanges burn their tokens regularly.
Less supply can support the price, if demand stays the same.
But burns aren't magic. If nobody wants the token, burning won't save it.
Follow for part 328: get-rich-quick traps. Not financial advice.
Turn one hundred into ten thousand in a month. Sounds familiar?
scenes.p: A flashy salesman on a stage spins a giant wheel of money while the crowd throws cash at him, the wolf leaving through the exit.

scenes.say: Fast money promises come in many forms: secret strategies, signals that never lose, guaranteed bots.
Real wealth is usually slow and boring.
Every loss on a get-rich-quick scheme is money that could have compounded for years.
If it's fast, easy and guaranteed, someone else is getting rich. Probably from you.
Follow for part 329: inflationary versus deflationary tokens. Not financial advice.

329.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 329.

scenes.say: Some tokens keep growing their supply. Others shrink it. Which is better?
scenes.p: Two balloons: one inflating bigger and bigger as coins pour in, the other slowly shrinking, the wolf holding both strings.

scenes.say: Inflationary tokens keep adding supply, through rewards or emissions.
Deflationary tokens reduce supply over time, through burns or a fixed cap.
Neither is automatically good. What matters is demand versus new supply.
Always check the emission schedule before you invest.
Follow for part 330: real yield. Not financial advice.

330.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 330.

scenes.say: Not all yield is real. Here's how to tell the difference.
scenes.p: The wolf holds a basket of real golden coins next to a basket of shiny paper coins blowing away in the wind.

scenes.say: Many DeFi yields are paid in newly printed tokens. That's not real income.
Real yield comes from actual revenue, like trading fees, paid in stablecoins or major coins.
It's usually lower, but more sustainable.
Ask where every percent comes from. If it's just new tokens, it's dilution.
Follow for part 331: insurance before investing. Not financial advice.
Before you invest a cent, protect what you can't afford to lose.
scenes.p: The wolf builds a solid brick house with a big umbrella-shaped roof protecting it from a storm.

scenes.say: Your health, your income, your home. That's what insurance is for.
One accident without insurance can wipe out years of investing.
Insurance is a cost, not an investment. Buy what you need, not what's sold hardest.
Protect first, then grow.
Follow for part 332: how stablecoin issuers make money. Not financial advice.

332.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 332.

scenes.say: Stablecoin companies can earn billions a year. Here's how.
scenes.p: A giant vault full of government bond certificates produces a steady stream of interest coins into a bucket, the wolf watching.

scenes.say: When you hold a stablecoin, the issuer holds your dollar in reserves.
They invest those reserves in safe assets, like government bills, and keep the interest.
With billions in reserves, that can mean billions in profit.
You get stability. They get the yield. Know that trade-off.
Follow for part 333: the role of Tether. Not financial advice.

333.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 333.

scenes.say: One stablecoin moves more money than many banks: Tether.
scenes.p: A huge green coin with a dollar symbol forms a bridge between two islands, crowds of traders crossing it, the wolf watching.

scenes.say: Tether's USDT is the biggest stablecoin in the world, launched in 2014.
It's used everywhere: trading, payments, and saving in dollars where local currencies are weak.
In the past, it faced questions and a legal settlement over its reserves.
Today it reports large holdings of US government bills, but you're still trusting a company.
Follow for part 334: taxes on investments, the basics. Not financial advice.
Making a profit is great. Then comes the tax.
scenes.p: The wolf sits at a desk with a calculator and a stack of forms while a polite tax officer takes a small slice of his coin pie.

scenes.say: In many countries, you pay tax when you sell an investment for more than you paid.
Dividends and interest are often taxed too.
Losses can sometimes reduce your taxes, and tax-advantaged accounts can help a lot.
Rules differ everywhere. Keep records, and ask a local professional.
Follow for part 335: crypto payments in daily life. Not financial advice.

335.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 335.

scenes.say: Can you actually buy groceries with crypto? Yes.
scenes.p: The wolf pays for groceries at a shop by tapping a crypto card, the cashier smiling, everyday scene.

scenes.say: You can pay through crypto debit cards, or directly with stablecoins.
Sending stablecoins abroad can be faster and cheaper than a bank transfer.
But spending crypto can be a taxable event, and prices move.
Many people spend stablecoins, and keep volatile coins for long-term savings.
Follow for part 336: Bitcoin as long-term savings. Not financial advice.

336.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 336.

scenes.say: Some people save in Bitcoin the way their grandparents saved in gold.
scenes.p: The wolf puts a small golden Bitcoin into a sturdy time capsule and buries it in his garden, a calendar showing many years.

scenes.say: They treat it as digital gold: a small part of savings, held for years.
They buy regularly, store it securely, and ignore short-term noise.
But it's still volatile. A long-term holder must accept drops of seventy percent or more.
Only save in Bitcoin what you can truly leave untouched for years.
Follow for part 337: how a stock chart differs from a crypto chart. Not financial advice.
Stock charts and crypto charts look alike. They're not.
scenes.p: Two big screens side by side: a calmer stock chart with gaps at night and a wild nonstop crypto chart, the wolf comparing them.

scenes.say: Stock charts have gaps: prices jump overnight, between the close and the next open.
Crypto never closes, so there are fewer gaps, but more weekend surprises.
And crypto usually moves several times more than big stocks.
The same tools work on both. Just adjust your stops to each market's volatility.
Follow for part 338: cold storage, step by step. Not financial advice.

338.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 338.

scenes.say: Cold storage, step by step.
scenes.p: The wolf walks carefully into an icy vault holding a small hardware wallet, snowflakes falling around him.

scenes.say: Buy a hardware wallet from the official store, and set it up yourself.
Write the seed phrase on paper or metal, and store it safely. Never digitally.
Send a small test amount first, then the rest.
Keep the device and the seed phrase in different places. That's cold storage.
Follow for part 339: testing your backup. Not financial advice.

339.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 339.

scenes.say: A backup you've never tested is a hope, not a backup.
scenes.p: The wolf runs a fire drill in his home office, holding a steel seed backup plate and a stopwatch.

scenes.say: With a small amount, practice restoring your wallet from the seed phrase on another device.
Check that the addresses match.
Then wipe the test device, and store everything safely again.
Do it once now, and you'll stay calm if your device ever breaks.
Follow for part 340: earnings season. Not financial advice.
Four times a year, the stock market gets its report card. It's earnings season.
scenes.p: A wall calendar covered in colorful company stickers under spotlights, the wolf with popcorn watching like it's a show.

scenes.say: Most big companies report their results within a few weeks.
Stocks can jump or fall ten percent or more in a day.
Big tech results can move the whole market, and even crypto.
If you hold individual stocks, know their dates, and avoid oversized positions before them.
Follow for part 341: what happens if your exchange gets hacked. Not financial advice.

341.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 341.

scenes.say: What happens to your coins if your exchange gets hacked?
scenes.p: Alarm lights flash outside a glowing exchange building while hooded figures run away with bags of coins, the wolf on the phone.

scenes.say: Exchanges have been hacked many times, from Mt. Gox to Bybit in 2025, which lost around one and a half billion dollars.
Some exchanges covered user losses. Others froze withdrawals, or went bankrupt.
So use reputable exchanges, and don't keep long-term savings there.
Spread your risk, and use your own wallet for what you plan to hold.
Follow for part 342: exchange insurance funds. Not financial advice.

342.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 342.

scenes.say: Some exchanges keep an emergency fund for their users. Does it protect you?
scenes.p: The wolf looks into a big glass emergency box on a wall filled with gold coins, a small hammer hanging next to it.

scenes.say: After hacks in the past, some exchanges created insurance funds, like Binance's SAFU fund in 2018.
They're meant to cover user losses after a hack or a failure.
But the size, the rules, and who decides to pay are set by the exchange itself.
It's a nice extra, not a guarantee. Keep only what you need on any exchange.
Follow for part 343: the business cycle. Not financial advice.
The economy moves in waves. It's called the business cycle.
scenes.p: The wolf surfs a giant wave shaped like an economic curve, rising and falling, over a city skyline.

scenes.say: Expansion: growth, jobs and profits rise.
Peak: everything looks great, and inflation often heats up.
Contraction: spending slows, profits fall, sometimes a recession.
Trough: the bottom, before the next expansion. Markets often turn before the economy does.
Follow for part 344: fake airdrops on social media. Not financial advice.

344.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 344.

scenes.say: Free tokens! Claim now! That post under a famous account is probably a trap.
scenes.p: A glowing suspicious gift box floating under a phone screen with a social media post, the wolf pushing it away with a cautious face.

scenes.say: Scammers reply to real accounts with fake airdrop links, using similar names and logos.
The site asks you to connect your wallet and sign. Then your tokens disappear.
Real projects announce airdrops on their official channels, never in random replies.
If you didn't expect it, don't click it.
Follow for part 345: deepfake scams. Not financial advice.

345.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 345.

scenes.say: That video of a famous billionaire giving away crypto? It's fake.
scenes.p: A giant screen shows a famous-looking businessman whose face is a glitching digital mask, the wolf pointing at the glitch.

scenes.say: Scammers use AI deepfakes to copy faces and voices of celebrities and CEOs.
They run fake live streams promising to double any crypto you send.
No real person will ever double your crypto. Ever.
Check the official account, and remember: if they ask you to send first, it's a scam.
Follow for part 346: consumer staples versus luxury. Not financial advice.
In a recession, people still buy toothpaste. They stop buying handbags.
scenes.p: The wolf pushes a shopping cart with basic groceries past a closed luxury boutique window.

scenes.say: Consumer staples are companies selling things we always need: food, soap, drinks.
Their sales stay steady, so their stocks are usually less volatile.
Luxury and discretionary companies sell things we want, which can boom or bust with the economy.
Many investors balance both, depending on the cycle.
Follow for part 347: AI trading bot scams. Not financial advice.

347.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 347.

scenes.say: An AI trading bot that never loses? It's not AI. It's a scam.
scenes.p: A shiny robot with a glowing brain on a flashy stage, while behind the curtain a man counts stolen money.

scenes.say: Scammers use the AI buzzword to sell bots with guaranteed daily profits.
They show fake dashboards with smooth gains, and ask you to deposit on their platform.
Withdrawals get blocked, or require an extra fee.
Real tools, AI or not, never promise guaranteed profits, and never need to hold your money.
Follow for part 348: job offer scams. Not financial advice.

348.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 348.

scenes.say: An easy online job: like videos, earn money. Then they ask you to deposit crypto.
scenes.p: The wolf sits at a laptop clicking like buttons on endless videos while a sinister shadow in the screen asks for coins.

scenes.say: Task scams start with small payouts, to build your trust.
Then you need to deposit to unlock bigger tasks or your earnings.
The more you deposit, the more they ask, and you never get it back.
A real job never asks you to pay to get paid.
Follow for part 349: healthcare stocks. Not financial advice.
People will always need medicine. That's why investors watch healthcare stocks.
scenes.p: The wolf in a white lab coat over his suit walks through a modern pharmaceutical lab with scientists and glowing test tubes.

scenes.say: Healthcare includes drug makers, medical devices, hospitals and insurers.
Demand is steady, and aging populations keep it growing.
But drug trials can fail, and patents expire, which can hit a stock hard.
Many investors use healthcare funds to spread these risks.
Follow for part 350: how to report a scam. Not financial advice.

350.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 350.

scenes.say: You got scammed. Here's what to do right away.
scenes.p: The wolf at a police station desk handing a folder of printed evidence to a kind officer.

scenes.say: Stop all contact, and don't send any more money, no matter what they promise.
Save everything: addresses, transaction IDs, screenshots, and chats.
Report it to the police, and to the exchange you sent from. They may be able to freeze funds.
Warn others, and beware of recovery scammers who will contact you next.
Follow for part 351: crypto and your mental health. Not financial advice.

351.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 351.

scenes.say: Crypto can mess with your head. Let's talk about it.
scenes.p: The wolf sits calmly on a therapist-style couch talking, while a stormy cloud of charts hovers above his head and starts to clear.

scenes.say: Constant price checking, big swings and losses can cause real stress and anxiety.
If crypto affects your sleep, your mood, or your relationships, that's a sign to step back.
Invest smaller, check less, and talk to someone you trust.
Your mental health is worth more than any coin.
Follow for part 352: energy stocks. Not financial advice.
When oil prices rise, one group of stocks often rises with them: energy.
scenes.p: The wolf on an oil rig platform holding a stock certificate, a bright sunrise over the sea.

scenes.say: Energy companies drill, refine and sell oil and gas.
Their profits swing with energy prices, so their stocks can be very cyclical.
Many pay big dividends when prices are high.
The shift to renewables adds long-term uncertainty, and new opportunities.
Follow for part 353: FOMO at all-time highs. Not financial advice.

353.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 353.

scenes.say: Everyone is posting the new all-time high. And you feel the urge to buy. Now.
scenes.p: The wolf stands at the top of a mountain-shaped chart where a crowd celebrates with fireworks, his paw hovering over a buy button.

scenes.say: FOMO peaks when prices are already high, and attention is everywhere.
Buying in a rush means buying with no plan, at the most emotional moment.
If you want exposure, buy a small part now, and plan the rest over time.
Missing a move costs nothing. Buying the top can cost a lot.
Follow for part 354: buying the dip. Not financial advice.

354.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 354.

scenes.say: Buy the dip. The most famous advice in crypto. But which dip?
scenes.p: The wolf stands at the edge of a dip in the road with a shopping bag, looking down a road that keeps going down further.

scenes.say: Buying after a drop can work well in a healthy uptrend.
But in a downtrend, every dip can be followed by a lower one.
Buy dips in stages, not all at once, and only in assets you'd hold for years.
And keep cash for the dips that are bigger than you expect.
Follow for part 355: bank stocks. Not financial advice.
Banks make money from a simple gap. Here's how bank stocks work.
scenes.p: The wolf stands behind a classic bank counter with two coin piles, a small one coming in and a bigger one going out as loans.

scenes.say: Banks pay you interest on deposits, and charge more on loans. The difference is their profit.
Rising rates can widen that gap, up to a point.
But in crises, bad loans and bank runs can sink them fast, like in 2008 and in 2023.
Big, well-capitalized banks are usually steadier than small risky ones.
Follow for part 356: catching a falling knife. Not financial advice.

356.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 356.

scenes.say: Never try to catch a falling knife. Here's what traders mean.
scenes.p: A cartoon kitchen knife falling from the sky toward the wolf's open paw, the wolf quickly pulling his paw back.

scenes.say: When a price is crashing hard, buying too early can hurt badly.
The price can keep falling much further than seems reasonable.
Wait for signs that selling is slowing: a base, a higher low, or a bounce that holds.
Being a bit late is cheaper than being very early.
Follow for part 357: the dead cat bounce. Not financial advice.

357.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 357.

scenes.say: The price bounces after a crash, and everyone thinks it's over. Sometimes, it's a dead cat bounce.
scenes.p: A deflated balloon cat bounces once off the ground and falls flat again, the wolf watching with a skeptical face.

scenes.say: A dead cat bounce is a short recovery inside a bigger downtrend.
Shorts take profit and bargain hunters buy, so the price jumps for a while.
Then sellers return, and the price makes new lows.
One green day isn't a trend. Wait for higher lows before believing it.
Follow for part 358: utility stocks. Not financial advice.
The most boring stocks on the market? Utilities. And that's their strength.
scenes.p: The wolf walks under tall power lines in the countryside at dawn, holding a steady glowing light bulb.

scenes.say: Utilities provide electricity, gas and water. People pay those bills in good and bad times.
They're often regulated, with steady profits and reliable dividends.
Because they carry a lot of debt, they're sensitive to interest rates.
Many investors use them for stability, not for fast growth.
Follow for part 359: capitulation. Not financial advice.

359.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 359.

scenes.say: The moment everyone gives up is often close to the bottom. It's called capitulation.
scenes.p: The wolf stands calmly in a stormy valley while a crowd waves white flags and runs away.

scenes.say: After a long decline, a final wave of panic selling hits, with huge volume.
Holders who swore they'd never sell finally sell.
Sellers run out, and the price can stabilize, or start to recover.
You'll only know it for sure afterwards. That's why buying in stages helps.
Follow for part 360: accumulation zones. Not financial advice.

360.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 360.

scenes.say: Big moves often start in silence, in an accumulation zone.
scenes.p: The wolf quietly fills a basket with coins in a calm, empty marketplace at dawn while everyone else sleeps.

scenes.say: After a big drop, the price moves sideways for weeks or months.
Interest is low, news is quiet, and patient buyers quietly build positions.
Volume is often low, until a breakout ends the range.
Boring markets can be the best time to plan, not to leave.
Follow for part 361: small caps versus large caps. Not financial advice.
Small companies or big ones? Small caps versus large caps.
scenes.p: The wolf stands between a small growing sapling and a giant old oak tree, comparing them.

scenes.say: Large caps are big, established companies. Usually steadier.
Small caps are smaller companies with more room to grow, and more risk.
Small caps can fall harder in recessions, and rise faster in recoveries.
Many investors hold mostly large caps, with a smaller slice of small caps.
Follow for part 362: distribution at the top. Not financial advice.

362.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 362.

scenes.say: The top of a market often looks like a party. It's called distribution.
scenes.p: A rooftop party with fireworks while a few well-dressed people quietly leave through the back door with bags of coins, the wolf noticing.

scenes.say: After a long rise, the price stops making progress and swings sideways at high levels.
Early buyers are quietly selling to late buyers.
The news is great, and everyone is talking about it.
When the euphoria is loudest, take some profit, and follow your plan.
Follow for part 363: why most altcoins lose against Bitcoin. Not financial advice.

363.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 363.

scenes.say: Most altcoins have lost value against Bitcoin over the long run. Here's why.
scenes.p: A long race track where a golden Bitcoin runner steadily keeps going while many colorful altcoin runners fall behind or drop out.

scenes.say: New altcoins launch constantly, competing for the same money.
Many have big token unlocks and inflation, which pressure the price.
Some altcoins outperform for a cycle, but few stay on top.
If you hold altcoins, compare them to Bitcoin, not just to the dollar.
Follow for part 364: international investing. Not financial advice.
Investing only in your own country? You might be missing most of the world.
scenes.p: The wolf spins a big globe with glowing stock markets on different continents.

scenes.say: Your country is only a small part of the global stock market.
Global funds spread your money across the US, Europe, Asia and emerging markets.
Different economies grow at different times, which smooths out the ride.
Watch out for currency risk and fees, and keep it simple.
Follow for part 365: the power of doing nothing. Not financial advice.

365.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 365.

scenes.say: Sometimes, the smartest move in investing is to do absolutely nothing.
scenes.p: The wolf sits calmly on a dock fishing at sunset while a storm of charts passes far away.

scenes.say: Every trade has a cost: fees, taxes, and the risk of being wrong.
Many investors hurt their returns by reacting to every headline.
Having a plan means you already know what to do, and often, that's nothing.
Patience is a position.
Follow for part 366: the trailing stop loss. Not financial advice.

366.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 366.

scenes.say: A stop loss that follows the price up. It's called a trailing stop.
scenes.p: The wolf climbs a staircase while a safety net follows one step below him, always rising with him.

scenes.say: You set a distance, like ten percent below the price.
As the price rises, the stop rises with it. If the price falls, the stop stays.
It protects profits without guessing the top.
Set it too tight, and normal swings kick you out. Leave room to breathe.
Follow for part 367: the Nikkei, the DAX and other world indexes. Not financial advice.
Every big country has its own stock market scoreboard. Here are the famous ones.
scenes.p: The wolf stands in front of a wall of world clocks and glowing scoreboards from different countries in a global trading room.

scenes.say: In the US, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq. In Japan, the Nikkei.
In Germany, the DAX, with forty of the biggest German companies.
In the UK, the FTSE 100. In Europe, the Euro Stoxx 50.
Watching them tells you how the world economy is feeling, region by region.
Follow for part 368: averaging up versus averaging down. Not financial advice.

368.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 368.

scenes.say: Your coin is down. Do you buy more? Your coin is up. Do you add? Averaging down versus up.
scenes.p: The wolf stands between two staircases, one going down into fog and one going up into sunlight, choosing carefully.

scenes.say: Averaging down means buying more as the price falls, lowering your average cost.
It works for quality assets in temporary dips. It's dangerous for broken projects.
Averaging up means adding to a winner as it proves itself.
Either way, set a maximum size first, so one position never takes over your portfolio.
Follow for part 369: stress testing your portfolio. Not financial advice.

369.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 369.

scenes.say: What would happen to your portfolio if crypto fell seventy percent tomorrow?
scenes.p: The wolf runs a crash test on a small car made of coins hitting a wall, watching from behind safety glass with a clipboard.

scenes.say: That's a stress test: imagining a bad scenario before it happens.
Calculate your losses if stocks fall forty percent and crypto seventy.
Could you live with it, without selling in panic, or needing that money?
If the answer is no, reduce your risk now, while it's calm.
Follow for part 370: a simple diversified portfolio. Not financial advice.
A simple diversified portfolio doesn't need dozens of investments.
scenes.p: The wolf arranges four neat glass jars on a shelf: a big one with stock coins, one with bond certificates, one with gold, and a small one with crypto.

scenes.say: A broad stock index fund for long-term growth.
Some bonds or cash for stability and emergencies.
Maybe a little gold, and a small slice of crypto if you accept the risk.
Simple, cheap, and easy to stick with. That's what wins over decades.
Follow for part 371: the biggest lessons so far, part three. Not financial advice.

371.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 371.

scenes.say: One more time, the biggest lessons of this series.
scenes.p: The wolf stands on a hill at sunset holding a big book of lessons, looking back at the long road he walked.

scenes.say: Protect yourself first: emergency fund, no expensive debt, and secure keys.
Invest regularly, keep costs low, and diversify.
Respect risk: small positions, stop losses when trading, no leverage when you're learning.
And beat your emotions with a written plan.
Follow for part 372: planning your exit for the next bull market. Not financial advice.

372.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 372.

scenes.say: The best time to plan your exit from a bull market is before it starts.
scenes.p: The wolf draws an exit map with several doors at different heights on a mountain, on a calm sunny day.

scenes.say: Decide in advance at what prices or signs you'll take profit.
Sell in steps, not all at once.
Decide where the profits go: cash, stablecoins, or other investments.
In a mania, nobody thinks clearly. Your past self, with a plan, will save you.
Follow for part 373: how billionaires really built wealth. Not financial advice.
How did billionaires really build their wealth? Not how social media tells you.
scenes.p: The wolf looks at a long timeline painted on a wall, with a small workshop at the start and a giant company tower at the end.

scenes.say: Most built a business, and owned a big piece of it for decades.
Others invested patiently and let compounding work, like Warren Buffett.
Very few got rich from a single lucky trade.
Ownership, patience and time. That's the real recipe.
Follow for part 374: what to do in a bear market. Not financial advice.

374.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 374.

scenes.say: The bear market is here. What do you do?
scenes.p: The wolf calmly works at his desk in a cozy cabin while a big grumpy bear wanders past the snowy window.

scenes.say: First, don't panic sell quality assets at the bottom.
If you have a plan and spare cash, keep buying slowly.
Use the quiet time to learn, research and prepare.
Bear markets build the fortunes that bull markets reveal.
Follow for part 375: staying safe for the next ten years. Not financial advice.

375.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 375.

scenes.say: How to keep your crypto safe for the next ten years.
scenes.p: The wolf locks a sturdy safe in a calm home office, a calendar on the wall showing many years ahead.

scenes.say: Use a hardware wallet, with your seed phrase backed up on metal in two places.
Keep your email and exchanges protected with an authenticator app.
Never share your seed phrase, never rush, and verify every address.
And make sure someone you trust knows how to find your instructions.
Follow for part 376: the power of patience in the stock market. Not financial advice.
The stock market rewards patience more than intelligence.
scenes.p: The wolf sits under a big tree that grows taller around him over the years, reading the newspaper calmly.

scenes.say: Over long periods, broad stock markets have gone up, despite crashes, wars and recessions.
Investors who stayed in through the bad years captured the recoveries.
Those who sold in panic often bought back higher, or never came back.
Time is your biggest advantage. Don't waste it trying to be clever.
Follow for part 377: building wealth slowly. Not financial advice.

377.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 377.

scenes.say: Getting rich slowly is not exciting. It's just what works.
scenes.p: The wolf lays bricks one by one, building a strong golden house over many seasons.

scenes.say: Save a part of every paycheck, automatically.
Invest it in simple, diversified, low-cost assets.
Increase it every time your income grows.
Ten, twenty, thirty years. That's how ordinary people build extraordinary wealth.
Follow for part 378: your checklist before every buy. Not financial advice.

378.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 378.

scenes.say: Before you buy any investment, run through this checklist.
scenes.p: The wolf holds a long glowing checklist and a pen in front of a shop window full of coins, thinking.

scenes.say: Do I understand what it is, and how it makes money?
How much of my portfolio will it be, and can I afford to lose it?
Where will I take profit, and when will I admit I'm wrong?
Am I buying because of a plan, or because of FOMO?
Follow for part 379: why most day traders lose. Not financial advice.
Most day traders lose money. That's not an opinion. It's what the studies show.
scenes.p: The wolf watches a room full of exhausted day traders staring at many screens, most of them red, at night.

scenes.say: Studies of real day traders have found that the vast majority lose money over time.
Fees, spreads and taxes eat small gains.
And they compete against professionals and algorithms.
If you trade, do it with a small part of your money, and invest the rest for the long run.
Follow for part 380: your checklist before every sell. Not financial advice.

380.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 380.

scenes.say: Before you sell, run through this checklist.
scenes.p: The wolf pauses with his paw above a red sell button, a checklist floating next to him, calm and thoughtful.

scenes.say: Has my reason for owning it changed, or just the price?
Am I selling because of a plan, or because of fear?
What are the taxes and fees of selling now?
And where will the money go next? Selling is only half the decision.
Follow for part 381: your security checklist. Not financial advice.

381.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 381.

scenes.say: Your crypto security checklist. Save this one.
scenes.p: The wolf stands in front of a vault door ticking off a glowing security checklist, padlocks and shields around him.

scenes.say: Seed phrase offline, on paper or metal, in two safe places.
Authenticator app on every exchange and email. No SMS codes.
Hardware wallet for savings, bought from the official store.
Bookmarks for important sites, no random links, and never share your screen with strangers.
Follow for part 382: dollar-cost averaging into index funds. Not financial advice.
The simplest long-term strategy in the stock market: index funds, every month.
scenes.p: The wolf drops one coin every month into a big transparent basket full of tiny company buildings, a calendar behind him.

scenes.say: You buy a broad index fund with the same amount, on the same day, every month.
No stock picking, no market timing.
When prices fall, your money buys more shares.
Low effort, low cost, and historically very hard to beat.
Follow for part 383: the ten commandments of crypto, part one. Not financial advice.

383.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 383.

scenes.say: The ten commandments of crypto. Part one.
scenes.p: The wolf holds up two big stone tablets in a dramatic mountain landscape, golden light breaking through clouds.

scenes.say: One: never invest more than you can afford to lose. Two: never share your seed phrase.
Three: no leverage while you're learning. Four: if it promises guaranteed returns, it's a scam.
Five: always have a plan before you buy.
The other five, in the next part.
Follow for part 384: the ten commandments of crypto, part two. Not financial advice.

384.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 384.

scenes.say: The ten commandments of crypto. Part two.
scenes.p: The wolf carves the last lines into a big stone tablet with a chisel, focused, mountain sunset.

scenes.say: Six: keep long-term savings in your own wallet. Seven: verify every address and link.
Eight: diversify, and keep most of your money in the most established assets.
Nine: don't let fear, greed or FOMO make decisions for you.
Ten: keep learning. The market changes. So should you.
Follow for part 385: investing in your twenties, thirties and forties. Not financial advice.
How to invest in your twenties, thirties and forties.
scenes.p: Three versions of the wolf side by side: a young one with a skateboard, one with a briefcase, and an older one with reading glasses.

scenes.say: In your twenties: build habits. Emergency fund, no expensive debt, invest small and often.
In your thirties: increase what you invest as your income grows, and protect your family.
In your forties: review your plan, diversify, and think about retirement seriously.
At any age, the best time to start was years ago. The second best is today.
Follow for part 386: how far you've come. Not financial advice.

386.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 386.

scenes.say: If you've watched this series from the start, look how far you've come.
scenes.p: The wolf stands on a mountain peak at sunrise looking back at the long winding path he climbed.

scenes.say: You know how blockchains, wallets and exchanges work.
You know how to spot scams, and protect your keys.
You know stocks, gold, bonds, and how the economy moves.
And most importantly, you know that patience and risk control beat hype.
Follow for part 387: your crypto plan for the next year. Not financial advice.

387.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 387.

scenes.say: Let's build your plan for the next twelve months.
scenes.p: The wolf pins a big year planner on the wall with twelve sections and colorful sticky notes, coffee in hand.

scenes.say: Decide how much you'll invest each month, and automate it.
Choose your mix, and write down your rules for buying, selling and rebalancing.
Schedule a review every three months, not every day.
Then let time do its job.
Follow for part 388: how to read the news like an investor. Not financial advice.
Headlines are designed to grab your attention, not to make you money.
scenes.p: The wolf reads a newspaper through special glasses that turn the dramatic headlines into calm simple notes.

scenes.say: Ask: is this new information, or just noise repeated loudly?
Ask: does it change the long-term value of what I own?
Ask: who benefits if I react right now?
Most news should change nothing in your plan.
Follow for part 389: the biggest investing mistakes of all time. Not financial advice.
The biggest investing mistakes of all time all have something in common.
scenes.p: The wolf walks through a museum of famous financial disasters: a tulip, a dot-com bubble, a crashed house of cards.

scenes.say: Tulips, the South Sea, dot-coms, Terra, FTX: people paid for hype, not value.
They used borrowed money, or trusted the wrong people.
And they couldn't imagine that prices could fall.
Learn from their mistakes, so you don't have to repeat them.
Follow for part 390: the road ahead. Not financial advice.

390.intro_say: How to invest in crypto. Part 390.

scenes.say: Part 390. Thank you for walking this road with the wolf.
scenes.p: The wolf walks into a golden sunrise on a long road, waving back at the viewer, a backpack on his shoulder.

scenes.say: Markets will keep changing. New coins, new crashes, new opportunities.
But the rules stay the same: protect yourself, think long term, and keep learning.
And the series keeps going, with new lessons every week.
Follow for part 391: why gold has been money for thousands of years. Not financial advice.
